audit.why: MC_WR_TABLES.mel.lillia = 62.5 on MC_REAL_GAMES 8. Eight games is far too thin to build advice on, so I left the number alone and did not let it drive any rewrite.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two of Lillia's abilities are assigned to the wrong slots. wants.foe[0] reads 'Spam W (Blooming Blows) and E (Watch Out!)'. Blooming Blows is Q; Watch Out! Eep! is W; E is Swirlseed. The same slot confusion runs through the prose as 'her W/E spam' (mid, whys[2], spikes[1]) and 'before she can W-kite away' (spikes[0], early) - the stacking move speed comes off Blooming Blows, which is Q.
audit.why: The entry already gets this right once, in whys[3] ('kites every trade with Blooming Blows move-speed'), so it contradicts itself. A reader tracking the wrong key is watching the wrong cooldown: Blooming Blows is 6/5.5/5/4.5/4, Watch Out! Eep! is 14/13/12/11/10, Swirlseed is 12 flat. Those are three completely different windows.
audit.corrected: Q Blooming Blows, W Watch Out! Eep!, E Swirlseed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry tells Mel to reflect the wrong ability. dosFull[1].t is 'Reflect Blooming Blows back the moment he commits' and wants.you[1] says 'Use Rebuttal (W) to eat her Q/W bounce projectiles'. Blooming Blows and Watch Out! Eep! are not projectiles - Q is a self-centred nova, W is an area nova. Swirlseed (E) is the only ability in Lillia's kit carrying the projectile flag.
audit.why: Rebuttal reflects projectiles. Holding it for a nova that will connect regardless burns Mel's only defensive layer for nothing, and it is a 38s cooldown at rank 1. Naming Swirlseed makes the reflect a real decision instead of a coin flip. dosFull[2].d has the same problem in reverse - it talks about Lillia whiffing Blooming Blows, which has nothing to sidestep.
audit.corrected: Swirlseed (E) is the reflect target and the only thing she can whiff.
sources: champ-data/_kits/mel.json (W Rebuttal: 'reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker')

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in the entry states the condition on Lilting Lullaby. Riot's R text: 'Lillia causes all enemies with Dream Dust on them to become Drowsy before falling asleep.' The entry instead frames level 6 as a reaction test - 'whoever lands their CC first wins the all-in, so save E to cancel her sleep windup' (spikes[2]) and 'save Solar Snare to interrupt her sleep windup' (mid).
audit.why: This is the matchup. Lullaby is not a skillshot to dodge and there is no windup to interrupt - it hits everyone already carrying her passive mark, from up to 1600 range. The counterplay is refusing to eat a single ability before she ults, which is a completely different behaviour from the one the entry teaches. Telling a player to hold Solar Snare to cancel it will get them slept.
audit.corrected: Lullaby only sleeps targets already marked by Dream-Laden Bough; stay unmarked and a 150/130/110s ultimate does nothing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Blooming Blows deals bonus true damage on its outer edge - 'dealing extra true damage on the edge' - and the entry never mentions it. _missing-interactions.json flags the same thing as 'resistances-invalidated'.
audit.why: It inverts the normal spacing instinct. Against most short-range AoE you want to be at the rim; against Blooming Blows the rim is the punished spot and MR does not blunt it. For a squishy mage deciding where to stand while last-hitting, that is a real, actionable difference.
sources: champ-data/_kits/lillia.json (Q: 'dealing extra true damage on the edge')

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry credits Lillia with sustain in four places: 'her passive DOT out-sustain your short pokes' (spikes[1], mid), 'passive burn out-sustain your short pokes' (whys[2]), and 'slip every short trade with her healing and burn' (early). Lillia has no heal and no sustain anywhere in her kit. Dream-Laden Bough is 'additional max Health damage over time' - it is damage, not healing.
audit.why: It sets the wrong item plan. A reader who believes Lillia out-sustains will reach for anti-heal that does nothing here, and will misread why short trades feel bad - it is her burn out-damaging the poke, not her healing through it.
audit.corrected: Out-damage, not out-sustain; passive burn, not healing.
sources: champ-data/_kits/lillia.json (P description; no heal flag anywhere in kitFlags)

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns gives no numbers, and breakdown.trading, tradeBad, dontsFull[2].d and report[3].t all state Rebuttal is 'gone for twenty seconds'. Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26.
audit.why: Twenty seconds is wrong by nearly double at rank 1 and is the number the reader uses to decide whether to spend the barrier on chip. Against a champion whose entire plan is chip, understating it is the most expensive possible error.
audit.corrected: Blooming Blows 6s to 4s, Swirlseed 12s flat, Watch Out! Eep! 14s to 10s, Lullaby 150/130/110, Rebuttal 38s at rank 1. Repaired in breakdown.cooldowns and breakdown.trading; the other three copies of the 'twenty seconds' sentence are not uniquely addressable - see notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer refers to Lillia as 'he'/'his' throughout - tldr 'your reflect makes his best spell a liability', breakdown.trading 'his farming spot', 'while he's locked', 'his answer', phases[3] 'once he's marked deep'.
audit.why: Straightforward correctness, and it is a tell that the whole block is template fill rather than matchup writing. The tldr string is shared byte-for-byte with the lucian entry.
audit.corrected: Fixed the pronouns in breakdown.trading, the one copy the applier can target.

edits.before: Lillia wins by landing Blooming Blows, denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Lillia wins by marking you with Dream Dust, kiting on Blooming Blows speed, and cashing it in with Lullaby.

edits.before: - Mel vs Lillia - Track: Lillia Blooming Blows. - Hold the reflect for his real spell. - No commits into Blooming Blows. - The ultimate closes arguments; it doesn’t open them.
edits.after: - Mel vs Lillia - Track: Lillia Lullaby. - Rebuttal answers Swirlseed, not Blooming Blows. - Unmarked by Dream Dust means her R cannot sleep you. - Stay off the Q rim.

edits.before: Stack Overwhelm with every hit — once he's marked deep, your execute math starts working. Track Blooming Blows before stepping up.
edits.after: Stack Overwhelm with every hit — and hug inside Blooming Blows rather than sit on its rim, where its damage turns true.

edits.before: - Lillia Blooming Blows: matchup-defining — Her kiting speed stacks — catch her early in the chase or not at all. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Rebuttal has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Blooming Blows: 6s falling to 4s — her kiting speed stacks off it, so catch her early in the chase or not at all. - Swirlseed 12s is the only projectile Rebuttal can answer. - Lilting Lullaby 150/130/110s, and it needs you already marked.

edits.before: Good trade: Snare through the wave onto his farming spot, fan two full Q volleys while he's locked, and step back with W ready before his answer comes off cooldown. Bad trade: Burning Rebuttal on chip damage and then standing in Blooming Blows range — your only defensive layer is gone for twenty seconds.
edits.after: Good trade: Snare through the wave onto her farming spot, fan two full Q volleys while she's locked, and step back with W ready before Swirlseed comes off its 12s cooldown. Bad trade: Burning Rebuttal on chip and then standing on the rim of Blooming Blows, where its damage turns true — the barrier is gone for 38 seconds.

edits.after: Her Blooming Blows speed stacks every time a spell of hers lands — catch her early in the chase or not at all.

edits.after: Reflect Swirlseed — it is her one real projectile

edits.after: Lillia whiffs Swirlseed and the lane briefly belongs to you again.

edits.before: That is Lillia’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Her passive marks you on any spell hit, and that mark is what her R needs.

edits.after: Lilting Lullaby only touches enemies already carrying her passive Dream Dust — stay unmarked and a 150s ultimate has nobody to sleep.

edits.after: Use Rebuttal (W) to eat Swirlseed (E), her only projectile, and the slow it carries

edits.after: Spam Q (Blooming Blows) and W (Watch Out! Eep!) to kite past your E range and mark you

edits.after: Q + Solar Snare online — root her and land free Overwhelm stacks before Blooming Blows speed carries her off.

edits.after: Golden Eclipse vs her Lullaby — but Lullaby only sleeps targets already carrying Dream Dust, so stay unmarked at 6.

edits.after: Levels 3-5 her Q and W spam plus passive burn out-damage your short pokes while she dances out of Solar Snare range.

edits.before: Lillia is an off-meta skirmisher who lives on kite, so your whole early game is about pinning her down. Level 1 you out-range her — chip with Q and your ranged auto, but don't overstep into her passive DOT. Your real window is level 2: with Q and Solar Snare (E) up, snare her mid-bounce and dump Overwhelm stacks before she W-kites out. Hold W to swallow her ability projectiles and the move-speed she uses to dance away, then accept that from level 3 she'll try to slip every short trade with her healing and burn.
edits.after: Lillia is an off-meta skirmisher who lives on kite, so your whole early game is about pinning her down. Level 1 you out-range her — chip with Q and your ranged auto, but don't overstep into her passive burn. Your real window is level 2: with Q and Solar Snare (E) up, snare her and dump Overwhelm stacks before Blooming Blows speed carries her out. Hold W for Swirlseed, the one projectile she owns, then accept that from level 3 she'll try to slip every short trade with movement and burn.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 are hers if you let them be — her W/E spam and passive DOT out-sustain your one-and-done pokes while she stays outside E range and never commits. Don't chase; that's exactly what feeds her kite. Bait her abilities, last-hit at max Q range, and wait for your E to land cleanly. At 6 it becomes a CC race: your Golden Eclipse detonates everything you've stacked, but her Lullaby (R) sleep flips the all-in if she lands it first, so save Solar Snare to interrupt her sleep windup or to pin her the instant she dashes in.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 are hers if you let them be — her Q and W spam plus passive burn out-damage your one-and-done pokes while she stays outside E range and never commits. Don't chase; that's exactly what feeds her kite. Bait her abilities, last-hit at max Q range, and wait for your E to land cleanly. At 6 her Lullaby only puts targets already carrying Dream Dust to sleep, so the counterplay is refusing to eat a spell before she ults, not dodging the cast — and it is 150s if she spends it.
